entityDescription:
COMEX pioneered in the development of equipment for human intervention in extreme environments: The group led the way in industrial deep diving in the oil and gas supply and service sector. At the height of its activities, hundreds of divers from COMEX worked at depths of more than 300 meters, using helium-based breathing mixtures. COMEX¿ robots and equipment operate successfully at depths over 1000meter. 

The developments in the field of deep-sea intervention naturally led COMEX to participate in the development and test of equipment for human spaceflight: 
COMEX was involved in the verification of the European shuttle HERMES of the manned space flight program under the auspices of ESA. In the frame of these activities it participated in the test and development of equipment for EVA and IVA in its Neutral Buoyancy Facilities. Members of the European astronaut corps trained microgravity EVA in COMEX¿ test pools on real scale mock-ups of HERMES and COLUMBUS. 
COMEX is involved in the study of the SeaOrbiter, a new generation of exploration vessel, which is developed in cooperation with NASA¿s undersea training program. SeaOrbiter has multi-level pressure modules, used to prepare the technologies for long distance journeys in confined habitats.

The HYPERBARIC EXPERIMENTAL CENTRE is designed for studying the effects of pressure (hyperbaric and hypobaric) and gases (oxygen, nitrogen, helium and hydrogen etc.) on biological samples and structural models. The laboratory is equipped with a fully automated hypobaric/hyperbaric bio-incubator for tests with all gases, including hydrogen. Our team has successfully conducted more than 5300 operations, including nearly 2700 predominantly physiological or technological experimental human dives. 

This expertise gives COMEX today the necessary tools to develop, verify and test life support equipment and structural models for human intervention in hostile environments.

entityDescription: AI: Aerospace Innovation GmbH (AI) in Berlin develops special high-technology solutions and applications for the national and European aerospace industry and related agencies. AI is a precursor for new and innovative technologies, a provider of environmentally friendly and cost-efficient rocket propulsion systems for terrestrial and orbital operation as well as a centre of competence for strategic and technological space-related questions. Due to a long-standing experience in research and education along with extensive and detailed experimental work, AI is characterised by a unique technical know-how in the area of space transportation system design, rocket propulsion and propellant combustion as well as value analyses, cost modelling and modelling of complex socio-economic relations. AI was launched as an evolution of the aerospace engineering and consultancy company AI: Aerospace Institute, Lo, Adirim and Partners, that was founded in May 2000 within the frame of the Technology Transfer Program at Berlin University of Technology (TUB). When AI was founded in 2007 in order to provide complete system solutions and products in the field of aerospace propulsion, the core activities of AI: Aerospace Institute were transferred to the new company. Today, the team of AI consists of eight employees and two consultants. The company presently focuses on space transportation and propulsion system investigations as well as trend analyses, while the range of activities includes numerical simulations of complex dynamic processes, e.g. solid and hybrid rocket motor combustion, feasibility investigations for new technologies and systems as well as development and manufacturing of demonstrators and prototypes for customised propulsion solutions.

The IDA supports business enterprises in operation and development of business activity, as well as in the implementation of restructuring processes, and plays a major role in increasing competitiveness of Polish industry. The broad spectrum of support instruments includes both financial products and non-financial assistance in implementation of projects, such as providing access to investment areas and production facilities within Special Economic Zones administered by the IDA. The Company also makes it possible for business partners to liaise in implementing innovative projects. As part of the Polish Development Fund Group, the IDA cooperates with major Polish institutions supporting enterprises and provides comprehensive solutions in response to the current needs and challenges faced by businesses.
Since 2016, IDA has been conducting a dedicated support program for Polish space companies: “Comprehensive support program for Polish space technology sector”. This program defines and divides all IDA activities in four fields:
•Human Resources development;
•New business projects;
•Promotion;
•Financial instruments.
In each defined field IDA has developed support mechanism. Since 2016 each year IDA together with Polish Space Industry Association organises internship program. Up to 15 companies can hire an intern chosen in a contest for six months, IDA covers up to 50% of costs of such internship. During three finished editions, all together 43 young specialist were hired by 21 companies. IDA has also started initiative Space Academy, which main idea is to enable young engineers retrain from other speciality to space technology sector. Using competences of Warsaw University of Technology, Military University of Technology and Space Research Centre Polish Academy of Science training focused on Satellite Integration Phases – 0/A/B/C/D is offered with partial financing of IDA. 
IDA supports national programs dedicated to start-up acceleration, one of them is European Satellite Navigation Competition 2016, Space3ac Acceleration Program 2016 or European Rover Challenge 2018. Recently IDA become partner of MyGalileoApp competition of European Global Navigation Satellite System Agency. Additionally to improve cooperation between Polish large companies and SME’s, IDA provides service in searching and selecting innovative project for large companies in specified fields. Such activity/contest is done together with industrial partners and it’s called ARP Innovation Pitch. Since 2016 we have organised 20 such contests. One of ARP Innovation Pitch was dedicated to space technology.

National promotion is implemented by organising large events: Satellite Forum 2017, European Space TechTransfer Forum 2019 or supporting existing ones: Space Sectore Forum (2016 and 2018). Since 2017 IDA has launched dedicated loan program for polish space companies. One of the financial support mechanisms is the Open Innovation Network project that involves animating and supporting technology transfer transactions to Polish SMEs sector. Enterprises can obtain the grants which refund up to 70% of costs invested in the purchase of innovative technologies. Project is financed form UE founds. entityDescription: Domenico Capolongo, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Physical Geography and Geomorphology at the University of Bari Aldo Moro, Italy. His research primarily focuses on geomorphological processes and hydrogeological risks, with particular attention to landslides and erosion in rapidly evolving landscapes. He employs advanced GIS and remote sensing techniques, integrating data from field surveys, drones, and satellite imagery with numerical modelling to analyze and predict hazardous processes. Professor Capolongo is involved in the PNRR project RETURN (REducing risks, enhancing ecosystem services, and fostering Resilient communities), which aims at risk reduction and sustainable land management in areas prone to hydrogeological instability. He has an extensive publication record, with numerous research papers and citations highlighting his significant contributions to the study of geomorphological hazards.
